A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same HERMES research. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices support comparison. Renamed modules and relocated material, including v1 Appendix D becoming v2 Appendix G, can be matched.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark experiments, token and computational cost measurements, module ablations, sensitivity analyses, and topic-level results.

after.justification: v2 retains original experiments and adds DeepSeek-V3.2 evaluations, HERMES@5 results, a human formalization audit, and repeated-run summaries.

M1.justification: v2 adds HERMES@5 inference variants that generate five HERMES traces and select using majority voting or Skywork (Section 5.2, Table 1). The underlying formalization, proof/counter-proof, memory, and feedback pipeline remains unchanged. Renaming the translation module and adding pseudocode do not themselves establish algorithm changes.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate MATH500, AIME’25, CollegeMath, and HARDMath2. The new audit examines intermediate outputs on existing benchmarks, without adding a distinct task, population, or input environment. DeepSeek-V3.2 expands model configurations rather than dataset coverage.

E2.justification: The eight baseline strategies remain CoT, majority voting, Skywork, ArmoRM, Shepherd, RLHFlow, Safe, and Safe*. Their revised CoT@5-prefixed labels preserve their identities. The added HERMES@5 rows are variants of the proposed method.

E3.justification: v2 adds DeepSeek-V3.2 configurations, five-trace HERMES selection protocols, and a human audit with proof-coverage and semantic-faithfulness metrics (Sections 5.1–5.2 and 5.7). These substantially expand the evaluation design. The existing 15-minute limit, 8,192-token budget, and default formalizer/prover sampling budgets remain.

E4.justification: Section 5.7 newly investigates formalization fidelity, verification coverage, tool-call frequency, and the topics of successful and unresolved steps. Appendix D adds six paired informal/Lean examples. Earlier module ablations, sampling sensitivity, failure distributions, and the corrected-problem case study are retained.

E5.justification: Unlike v1's point estimates, v2 Appendix E/Table 7 reports means and standard deviations over five independent runs for nine inference methods, four base models, and two benchmarks. This introduces substantial uncertainty reporting; it does not establish an increase from any previously specified run count.

E6.justification: v2 adds DeepSeek-V3.2, HERMES@5, audit, and repeated-run results. For example, Table 1 newly reports Qwen3-8B/HERMES@5+Skywork at 43.3% on AIME, alongside the retained HERMES@1 result of 30.0%. Figure 3 revises Qwen3-8B/HERMES HM2 token usage from 10.6K to 7.7K. Replacing main-table V3.1 results with V3.2 results is a model-setting change, not a same-setting performance gain.

T1.justification: v2 Section 4.5 introduces Theorem 4.1 and a proof deriving O(N^2 + KTN^2) inference complexity, followed by an asymptotic comparison with ORM and PRM methods. v1 contains empirical FLOP accounting but no corresponding complexity theorem or proof.

C1.justification: The central contributions of intermediate Lean verification and contextual memory remain. v2 adds test-time scalability to its contribution claims. The abstract revises the highlighted accuracy improvement from 67% to 40% and claims a further 20% improvement from HERMES@5; the introduction changes its stated average gain from 14% to 23%.

C2.justification: v2 interprets increased tool calls on harder problems as greater reasoning decomposition and extends the earlier Mathlib-based domain explanation using audited success and failure patterns. It also discusses compatibility with reward-based selection and potential applicability beyond mathematics and Lean. The earlier geometry limitation remains.

D1.justification: Appendix F adds pseudocode and specifies cosine-similarity retrieval. Section 5.1 discloses thinking/non-thinking modes, without establishing changes to previously used modes. Appendix A removes the separate NO VERIFICATION response from the tool instructions. Core component versions, default budgets, and code-access information remain.

R1.justification: v2 adds references to the DeepSeek-V3.2 report and the Lean Community's Mathlib documentation. The related-work discussion and principal novelty positioning remain substantially unchanged; switching from numbered to author-year citations is stylistic.

P1.justification: v2 renames translation terminology to formalization, shortens several experimental discussions, adds a problem-formulation section, and reorganizes the appendices around added material. Author/affiliation wording and citation style also change. Most existing narrative is retained rather than extensively rewritten.

P2.justification: The main paper changes from a single-column layout to a two-column conference format, with substantial figure and table relocation and resizing. Table 1 expands, Figures 3 and 5 add HERMES@5 bars, and new audit/statistical tables, six formalization figures, and an algorithm display materially expand the presentation.

improvement.justification: The five-run uncertainty estimates and direct formalization audit make reliability more assessable than in v1, while pseudocode improves inspectability. These benefits support a limited net improvement. Reporting inconsistencies constrain the gain: audit sample counts are unclear, and the new DeepSeek-V3.2 HM2 results rank HERMES above Skywork in Table 1 (33.6% versus 30.8%), while Table 13's topic counts total 64 versus 65, reversing that ordering without explanation.
